To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
type-1 and -2alpha CRHR mRNA are differentially altered in the PVN under various physiological conditions.
CRHR- 1 and CRHR2alpha mRNA are expressed differentially in the PVN of the rat hypothalamus and are differentially regulated by stress and adrenocortical hormones.
CRH type-2alpha mRNA is expressed in the paraventricular hypothalamic nucleus of the rat, and its expression level is not changed by lipopolysacchride, corticosterone or adrenalectomized treatment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of CRH receptor expression in the PVNs in rats with liposaccharide (lip) injection, cortisone (cor) administration or adrenectomized (adx)
the regulation of corticotropin releasing hormone (CRH) in the hypothalmo-hypophyseal system
the role of CRH in the hypothalamo-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CRH-2 alpha mRNA is expressed in a distinct distribution from CRH-1 mRNA and that its expression is differentially regulated by various stressors.
the CRHR-1 gene is up-regulated by LPS and CORT, and down-regulated by adrenalectomy.
the CRHR-1 gene is regulated by stress and glucocorticoid and that CRHR- 2alpha mRNA is expressed constitutively in the PVN and is not altered by stress and glucocoicoid.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
(1) CRHR-2 is expressed in the PVN; (2) the CRHR-1 expression in the PVn is regulated by stress, CORT administration, adrenalectomy; and (3) the CRHR2alpha is not altered by these treatments.
CRH is regulated by the autonomic nervous system, the HPA axis, and the autocrine/paracrine system in a complex and dynamic manner.
CRH is the most important factor in the regulation of CRH mRNA and CRH-R1 mRNA in the hypothalamus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are two distinct CRHRs, CRHR-1, and CRHR- 2alpha, that are differentially regulated by LPS and stress in the PVN.
the CRHR-1 receptor is a key mediator of stress responses in the PVN and that CRHR- 2alpha receptor may be a key mediator of CRH release from CRH neurons.
there are two different receptors for CRH in the brain.
